_description: USC Department Clearance dataset for PlanSC Module 4B. Surfaces plain-language instructions to undergraduate students when a course requires departmental clearance (D-clearance) to enroll. Graduate D-clearance processes are out of scope.
_notes: All entries sourced from official USC department/school advising pages. 'verified' field indicates whether contact details and process steps have been manually confirmed against the live page. Always cross-check before production use — advising processes change each semester.

departments.priority_note: Declared CSCI majors get first priority and are processed starting March 23. BUAI and partner/joint program students are processed later starting April 20. Students outside these programs cannot request undergraduate CSCI D-clearance.
departments.clearance_required_for: Only specific CSCI courses require undergraduate D-clearance — not all CSCI courses. For Fall 2026, only CSCI 426 and CSCI 491A require D-clearance for the entire registration period. Always check the 'D' suffix on the 5-digit section number in Schedule of Classes and WebReg to confirm.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: The process depends on your major: (1) Declared CSCI majors: submit your request via the myViterbi D-Clearance Request Manager at myviterbi.usc.edu. (2) BUAI majors, partner/joint program majors, Pre-Engineering, and Pre-CS students: your home department advisor will provide a Microsoft Form starting March 16th each spring registration cycle — do not use myViterbi. Submissions from students outside these programs will be deleted. For Microsoft Form questions, email csdept@usc.edu. Pre-Engineering/Pre-CS students can also contact viterbi.studentservices@usc.edu. Do NOT contact the course instructor for D-clearance — instructors do not issue it.
departments.typical_turnaround: CSCI majors: requests open ~March 16, processing begins ~March 23. Partner/joint program students: processing begins ~April 20. D-clearance expires within a few days of being granted — register on Web Registration immediately.
departments.tips: D-clearance does not guarantee a seat. The myViterbi and Web Registration systems are not connected — you must register yourself on WebReg after receiving your approval email. Do not wait to register; if you miss the expiration date you go to the bottom of the queue. You cannot view your waitlist position, but you can see total pending requests per course in myViterbi's Summary Report.

departments.dept_name: Business Administration (Marshall General — BUAD, BAEP, BUCO, FBE, DSO, MOR, MKT)
departments.priority_note: Declared Marshall students get priority. Non-Marshall students may enroll in up to 3 Marshall courses before being admitted to a Marshall major or minor.
departments.clearance_required_for: Most Marshall courses are open enrollment (R-clearance) through the first week of class. Courses switch to D-clearance at the end of Week 1. ACCT 370 and ACCT 371 (Leventhal) are D-clearance for the entire registration period.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: After Week 1, obtain permission from the course instructor. If the instructor approves, they will notify the relevant advising office. For Leventhal (ACCT) courses: contact your Leventhal academic advisor or email leventhalug@marshall.usc.edu. For general Marshall courses: contact the Office of Undergraduate Advising and Student Affairs at undergrad.advising@marshall.usc.edu or call 213-740-0690. There are no centralized waitlists — you can add your name to an interest list through the advising office.
departments.typical_turnaround: Varies by instructor; advising office responds within 2–3 business days
departments.tips: Marshall instructors cannot add students to a section that is already full — D-clearance alone does not guarantee a seat.

departments.dept_name: Communication / Journalism / Public Relations (Annenberg — COMM, JOUR, PREL, ASCJ)
departments.priority_note: Declared Annenberg majors get priority and are cleared during mandatory advisement before registration opens. Non-majors can only request D-clearance after the mandatory advisement period ends.
departments.clearance_required_for: COMM courses require D-clearance starting Week 3 of the semester. JOUR and PREL courses require D-clearance starting Week 2.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Annenberg majors: request D-clearance during your mandatory advisement appointment each semester before registration opens. After mandatory advisement, requests can be made by phone or email to ascjadv@usc.edu. Non-majors: an online D-clearance form becomes available after the mandatory advisement period ends — contact ascjadv@usc.edu to ask when it opens. For closed courses after the cutoff week: email the professor with your full name, USC ID, and the 5-digit section number; the professor will forward approval to the Annenberg department.
departments.typical_turnaround: Approval confirmed within ~24 hours once instructor signs off; not guaranteed
departments.tips: D-clearance seat counts don't always match what's visible in Schedule of Classes — seats may be allocated before they appear open. Freshmen, sophomores, recently admitted majors, and students on academic probation must meet with an advisor before registration.

departments.dept_name: Film & Television Production / Cinema & Media Studies / Interactive Media (SCA — CTPR, CTCS, CTIN, CTAN)
departments.priority_note: Declared SCA students get priority. Non-SCA students can request but enrollment is very competitive and not guaranteed — non-major D-clearance requests only open after a date announced each semester.
departments.clearance_required_for: Almost all SCA undergraduate courses require D-clearance. Use the course prefix to find the right contact.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Contact the appropriate undergraduate office by course prefix: CTCS (Cinema & Media Studies): nonmajor@cinema.usc.edu | CTIN (Interactive Media): USCInteractive@cinema.usc.edu | CTPR (Film & TV Production): studentaffairs@cinema.usc.edu. Non-majors may submit D-clearance requests after a date announced each semester — check cinema.usc.edu/studentaffairs/dclearance.cfm for the current timeline.
departments.typical_turnaround: 5–7 business days; plan ahead
departments.tips: Good entry-point courses open to non-majors: CTCS 190 (Intro to Cinema) and CTCS 466 (Theatrical Film Symposium). For CNTV 495 (internship credit), secure the internship first, then submit the Internship D-Clearance Form via SCA Community.

departments.priority_note: Declared Thornton majors and minors get priority through their assigned advisor. Non-Thornton students are not listed as eligible for most courses — contact thornton.studentaffairs@usc.edu to ask about availability.
departments.clearance_required_for: Most Thornton undergraduate courses require D-clearance. Look for the 'D' suffix on the 5-digit section number in Schedule of Classes.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Thornton majors: D-clearances are issued during your mandatory academic advisement appointment each semester — you must meet with your assigned advisor before you can register. Thornton minors: submit a D-clearance request to thornton.studentaffairs@usc.edu; they will email you once it is processed. For individual instruction courses (300/301/501 level): use the D-clearance request forms on the Thornton Student Affairs page. After approval, register yourself on Web Registration — your advisor grants clearance only, not enrollment.
departments.typical_turnaround: Varies; D-clearances issued during priority advisement weeks expire at the end of that registration period
departments.tips: Submitting the D-clearance request form does not guarantee approval and does not automatically enroll you. Always register on Web Registration after receiving your approval confirmation email.

departments.clearance_required_for: All GESM sections require D-clearance. The GE office also manages enrollment for specific sections of GE departmental courses listed above. For all other Dornsife courses, D-clearance is handled by the department — see the Dornsife D-Clearance hub.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Process depends on class standing and semester: (1) Summer 2026 (all students): email gened@usc.edu with your name, USC ID, five-digit GESM section number, and indicate the request is for Summer 2026. (2) Fall 2026 — Freshmen (31 units or fewer): register directly on Web Registration if a seat is available — no GE office assistance needed. (3) Fall 2026 — Sophomores and above (32+ units): email gened@usc.edu on or after July 13 with your name, USC ID, and five-digit section numbers for your top five GESM choices. The GE office will respond within 2 business days. If granted, a D-clearance will be issued that also guarantees a seat — D-clearances cannot be granted for closed sections. For WRIT 150 questions, contact writprog@usc.edu.

departments.tips: Unlike most D-clearances, a GESM D-clearance guarantees a seat — it cannot be issued for already-closed sections. Freshmen may not take WRIT 150 and a GESM simultaneously in the fall semester; this is allowed in spring. Sophomores who haven't completed either may take both concurrently in any semester. Unoccupied GE seats are released on August 21st.

departments.how_to_get_clearance: Process depends on the course: (1) NEUR 490 (Directed Research): submit the NEUR 490 application form — find it at the application link. You must find a faculty sponsor whose lab conducts neuroscience research, develop a research proposal with them, and submit by 5:00pm on Friday of the first week of classes. Start at least one month before the deadline. Your faculty sponsor must sign the form electronically or send a separate approval email. Once approved by the Neuroscience Major Co-Directors, D-clearance will be granted. Submit using the Google Form at docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfKjIcJL0brEsv9SE0zOGrJmvOj1E3Gz4pfsBUs50SDOBbENw/viewform. (2) NEUR 493 (Neuroscience Honors Seminar): request approval from Zoe Lo at zhaolo@usc.edu.
departments.typical_turnaround: NEUR 490: allow approximately one week after submission for a decision from the Co-Directors. NEUR 493: not specified.
departments.tips: For NEUR 490, start finding a faculty sponsor at least 3 weeks before the application deadline — faculty are busy and may not respond quickly. The project must involve neuroscience research specifically; biology or psychology projects that do not investigate neural mechanisms will not qualify. Each unit of NEUR 490 requires 4 hours per week in the lab. Honors students (GPA 3.5+) should also consider NEUR 493 and NEUR 494. For help finding a sponsor, visit ngp.usc.edu/faculty/ to browse faculty by research topic.

The department can only issue D-clearance for CHE on-campus courses — not DEN sections. For D-clearance in other departments' courses (BME, CEE, CSCI, EE, ENE, ISE), contact those departments directly via myViterbi.
departments.contact_email: See myViterbi for submission; consult your advisor for course approval first
departments.contact_office: USC Viterbi — Mork Family Department of Chemical Engineering and Materials Science
departments.typical_turnaround: 3–4 business days
departments.tips: Pay attention to departmental announcements on myViterbi indicating when non-major students are eligible to request D-clearance — submitting before the window opens may not be processed. The Mork Family Department cannot issue D-clearance for other departments' courses, even if those courses appear on your degree plan.

departments.dept_name: Journalism / Public Relations (Annenberg — JOUR, PREL, ASCJ)
departments.priority_note: Declared JOUR and PREL majors get priority and are cleared during mandatory advisement before registration opens. Non-majors can only request via the online form after the mandatory advisement period ends (historically mid-April for fall, mid-November for spring). Non-majors are capped at 20 JOUR units and 20 COMM units total.
departments.clearance_required_for: All JOUR and PREL sections require D-clearance from the first day of class — earlier than COMM courses which stay open through the first week. Check the 'D' suffix on the section number in Schedule of Classes.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Process depends on your major: (1) Declared JOUR and PREL majors: D-clearance is issued during your mandatory advisement appointment each semester before registration opens. You must meet with an advisor during the advisement period (October–mid-November for spring, late February–mid-April for fall). (2) Non-majors: complete the online JOUR/PR D-clearance form, which is released to non-majors only after majors are served. Contact ascjadv@usc.edu to ask when it opens. Allow 24 hours for processing. D-clearances are issued every Wednesday and Friday; check WebReg > My Info > Cleared Sections. (3) For a closed course after the cutoff: email the professor with your full name, USC ID, and the 5-digit section number; the professor will forward approval to the department.
departments.typical_turnaround: ~24 hours once the form is submitted; clearances processed every Wednesday and Friday
departments.tips: JOUR/PREL sections switch to D-clearance on day one of classes — earlier than COMM. D-clearances expire (historically November 30 for fall) — if you miss the window you must re-request. Submitting the form does not guarantee clearance; it is issued based on program, class standing, and graduation date first, then first-come-first-served. An open seat does not guarantee clearance.

departments.priority_note: Declared Leventhal accounting majors and minors get priority. Non-Leventhal students may take a maximum of 12 units from Marshall/Leventhal before being admitted to a major or minor. ACCT 370 and ACCT 371 are D-clearance for the entire registration period.
departments.clearance_required_for: ACCT 370 and ACCT 371 are D-clearance at all times. Most other ACCT courses switch to D-clearance at the end of Week 2. Directed research and special courses are D-clearance at all times.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: For ACCT 370 and 371 and all other ACCT D-clearance courses: contact your Leventhal academic advisor or email leventhalug@marshall.usc.edu. For closed ACCT courses after Week 2: obtain permission from the course instructor first; if approved, the instructor notifies the Leventhal office.
departments.typical_turnaround: 2–3 business days
departments.tips: ACCT 370 and 371 are D-clearance the entire semester — do not wait until Week 2 to request. Non-Leventhal students should confirm eligibility with leventhalug@marshall.usc.edu before requesting. Instructor permission alone is not sufficient — the Leventhal office must process the clearance.

departments.dept_name: Business of Entertainment, Media and Technology / Entrepreneurship (Marshall — BAEP)
departments.priority_note: Declared Marshall Entrepreneurship and Innovation (BEI) majors get priority. BAEP 495 is D-clearance at all times. Most BAEP electives switch to D-clearance after Week 1.
departments.clearance_required_for: BAEP 495 (Entrepreneurship Practicum) is D-clearance at all times. BAEP 451, 452, 453, 454, and 460 have their own D-clearance process. Most other BAEP electives switch to D-clearance at the end of Week 1.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Contact the Lloyd Greif Center for Entrepreneurial Studies at entrepreneur@marshall.usc.edu. For BAEP 451/452/453/454/460, check the BAEP website for the specific process each semester.
departments.contact_office: Lloyd Greif Center for Entrepreneurial Studies — Hoffman Hall (HOH)
departments.typical_turnaround: 2–3 business days
departments.tips: BAEP uses a different contact than the general Marshall advising office — email entrepreneur@marshall.usc.edu, not undergrad.advising@marshall.usc.edu.

departments.priority_note: Declared Marshall students get priority. BUCO electives (and BUAD 302, WRIT 340) switch to D-clearance at the end of Week 1 — earlier than most other Marshall prefixes which stay open through Week 2–3.
departments.clearance_required_for: BUCO electives and BUAD 302 switch to D-clearance at the end of Week 1. FBE, MKT, MOR, DSO electives (300–499) generally stay R-clearance (open) for the first three weeks. Directed research (BUAD 490), internships (BUAD 495), field projects (BUAD 498), honors (BUAD 493/494), and international study courses are D-clearance at all times.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Email the Office of Undergraduate Advising at undergrad.advising@marshall.usc.edu with your full name, USC ID, USC email, course number, major, and graduating semester. For courses outside BUCO (FBE, MKT, MOR, DSO), the same office handles clearance. For BUAD 490/495 directed research and internships, a dedicated form is required — ask undergrad.advising@marshall.usc.edu for the form.
departments.typical_turnaround: 2–3 business days
departments.tips: BUCO courses close to D-clearance at the end of Week 1 — earlier than FBE/MKT/MOR/DSO which stay open through Weeks 2–3. BUAD 490 and BUAD 495 require a separate dedicated form, not just an email. This entry also covers FBE, DSO, MOR, and MKT prefixes — all route to undergrad.advising@marshall.usc.edu.

departments.priority_note: Architecture majors get priority. D-clearances are granted on a first-come, first-served basis. Non-Architecture students can request but enrollment in major-restricted studios is very limited.
departments.clearance_required_for: ARCH courses with a 'D' suffix on the 5-digit section number require D-clearance. Courses with an 'R' suffix are open enrollment. Each semester, students receive a Permit to Register with an assigned date and time for the following semester.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Submit the online D-clearance request form at arch.usc.edu/d-clearance. D-clearance is separate from prerequisite waivers — if you need a prereq waived, that is a separate request. For CPT/ARCH 524 (Professional Practicum internship credit): complete the CPT Application Form, bring it with your job offer letter to Architecture Student Services in person to obtain advisor approval and D-clearance, then return the form to the Office of International Services.
departments.contact_office: Architecture Student Services Office — Watt Hall (WAH)
departments.typical_turnaround: Not specified; allow at least 2–3 business days
departments.tips: D-clearance and prerequisite waivers are separate — submit both if needed. Prerequisite waivers for ARCH 410/525/526 are granted only rarely. The 5-year Bachelor of Architecture program starts only in fall semesters — if you are considering changing into this major, start the conversation with your advisor early given the time-to-degree implications.

departments.dept_name: Dance (USC Glorya Kaufman School of Dance)
departments.priority_note: Declared Kaufman BFA students get priority. Non-Kaufman students can take select open courses but technique course placement levels restrict access — students with prior experience who have not taken DANC 103 must contact uscdance@usc.edu for both a prerequisite waiver and D-clearance.
departments.clearance_required_for: DANC courses with a 'D' suffix on the section number. DANC 490 (Directed Research) always requires a separate proposal/approval process.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Process depends on the course: (1) Most DANC D-clearance courses: contact Kaufman Student Affairs at uscdance@usc.edu or call (213) 740-9327. D-clearance is managed through the School of Dance to ensure prerequisites are met and enrollment is managed. (2) DANC 490 (Directed Research, 1–16 units, for undergraduate majors or minors): submit a proposal for research or performance-related work on a topic not currently in the Kaufman catalog, culminating in a substantial piece of writing, performance, or other project. Proposals are reviewed by the Assistant Dean of Faculty in consultation with faculty — allow 5–8 business days. Students are notified by email; D-clearance to register online is issued after approval.
departments.contact_office: USC Glorya Kaufman School of Dance — Glorya Kaufman International Dance Center
departments.typical_turnaround: DANC 490: 5–8 business days. Other courses: not specified; allow 2–3 business days.
departments.tips: For DANC 490, the project must cover a topic not currently in Kaufman's course offerings — check the catalog before proposing. For technique courses, students with prior dance experience who skip DANC 103 must request both a prerequisite waiver and D-clearance in the same email to uscdance@usc.edu.

departments.dept_name: Dramatic Arts (USC School of Dramatic Arts — THTR)
departments.priority_note: Declared SDA students (BFA and BA) get priority and many courses carry explicit restrictions (e.g. 'Registration open to: School of Dramatic Arts'). Non-SDA students can request for courses without major restrictions but clearance is not guaranteed. Some courses require an instructor interview.
departments.clearance_required_for: THTR courses with a 'D' suffix on the section number. Many THTR sections carry school or major restrictions in Schedule of Classes.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Process depends on timing: (1) Before the first day of classes: submit the D-clearance request online at sdastudents.usc.edu — select 'D-Clearance Course request.' Online requests are accepted until noon on the Wednesday before the first day of classes. (2) From the first day of classes onward: obtain the SDA D-Clearance Approval form from sdastudents.usc.edu or in person at the Drama Center (DRC 104), get the instructor's signature, and return the completed form to DRC 104. (3) Some courses require an instructor interview — check the course notes in Schedule of Classes.
departments.contact_office: Office of Admissions and Student Services — Drama Center (DAB) 301
departments.typical_turnaround: Not specified; submit well before the registration deadline
departments.tips: The online portal (sdastudents.usc.edu) closes at noon the Wednesday before the first day of class — after that, you need the paper form with instructor signature. Always check the course restriction note in Schedule of Classes before requesting — many THTR sections are restricted to SDA students only and clearance will not be granted to non-SDA students regardless.

departments.dept_name: Art (USC Roski School of Art and Design — ARLT, RADS, FINE)
departments.priority_note: Declared Roski majors and minors get priority and use password-protected webforms during mandatory advising. Non-Roski students use a separate public form that opens weeks later. After Week 3 all sections switch to D-clearance and most non-major requests will not be approved.
departments.clearance_required_for: Roski courses with a 'D' suffix on the section number. All Roski sections convert to D-clearance in Week 3 — after that point most requests are not approved. Courses with an 'R' suffix are open enrollment.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Process depends on your status: (1) Roski majors: during mandatory advising, submit through the password-protected Roski major D-clearance webform (link and password emailed to all majors). Phone and email requests are NOT accepted during mandatory advising. Requests processed first-come, first-served during normal business hours. Each D-clearance is section-specific — if you want multiple sections of the same course, submit a separate request for each. (2) Roski minors: same password-protected process via the Roski minor webform (separate from the major form). (3) Non-Roski undergraduates: submit via the public (non-password) non-Roski D-clearance webform, which opens later in the semester (check roski.usc.edu for current dates). After the non-major form closes (~Week 3), email Antonio Bartolome at anbartol@usc.edu with a recent instructor email confirming seat availability. (4) Weeks 1–2 for any student: Roski Student Services will consider requests only if you can provide a recent instructor confirmation email AND there are available seats; seat cap increases require the Roski Dean's approval.
departments.contact_email: anbartol@usc.edu (non-major requests after form closes); roski@usc.edu (general)
departments.typical_turnaround: Processed during normal business hours; D-clearances expire on a set date each semester (e.g. Dec. 5 for Spring 2026) — register immediately after approval
departments.tips: D-clearances expire on a hard date each semester — if you miss it, you must re-request and go to the bottom of the queue. Each clearance is section-specific; one request does not cover multiple sections of the same course. D-clearance and prerequisite waivers are separate processes at Roski — submit both if needed.

departments.dept_name: Social Work (USC Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work — SOWK)
departments.priority_note: Registration is first-come, first-served within appointment times. Program Director must review and approve all D-clearance requests before clearance is issued. Schedule changes after the first week of classes are not likely to be approved.
departments.clearance_required_for: SOWK courses with a 'D' suffix on the section number. Schedule changes after Week 1 must be processed through Enrollment Services and are unlikely to be approved.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Email Enrollment Services at sdp.enroll@usc.edu to request D-clearance. The request will be reviewed by the designated Program Director before clearance is issued. Non-enrolled students (Limited Status) must complete a Limited Status form and submit it to the same address; the section must have space and the Program Director must approve.
departments.contact_office: USC Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work — Enrollment Services
departments.typical_turnaround: Not specified; allow at least 3–5 business days for Program Director review
departments.tips: Program Director approval is required — this takes longer than a simple email acknowledgment. Do not wait until the last minute. Schedule changes after Week 1 go through the same office but are unlikely to be approved.

departments.dept_name: Gerontology (USC Leonard Davis School of Gerontology — GERO)
departments.priority_note: No explicit priority tiers documented publicly — contact the school directly.
departments.clearance_required_for: GERO courses with a 'D' suffix on the section number. GERO 490x and 491/495 (directed research and practicum) always require advisor and faculty approval.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Contact the Leonard Davis School undergraduate advising office at ldsgero@usc.edu or call (213) 740-5156. For GERO 490x and 491/495 directed research/practicum courses, arrange with a faculty member and your advisor first before requesting D-clearance.
departments.contact_office: USC Leonard Davis School of Gerontology
departments.typical_turnaround: Not specified; allow at least 2–3 business days
departments.tips: No standalone D-clearance process page is publicly documented for Gerontology — always check the current Schedule of Classes note for the specific section, which may name a contact person. For directed research courses, start conversations with faculty well before registration opens.

departments.dept_name: Media Arts / Interdisciplinary Studies (GE Office — MDA, INDS, FESM)
departments.priority_note: Sophomores and above must request via email. Freshmen (31 units or fewer) can register directly on WebReg for GESM if a seat is available — same policy applies to MDA and INDS GE sections.
departments.clearance_required_for: MDA, INDS, and FESM course prefixes are managed by the GE office, not by individual departments. All sections with a 'D' suffix require D-clearance through the GE office.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Email the GE office at gened@usc.edu with your name, USC ID, and the five-digit section number(s) you are requesting. For Summer sections, indicate that the request is for Summer in your email. For Fall sections (sophomores and above), email on or after the date announced by the GE office each spring. The GE office will respond within 2 business days.
departments.typical_turnaround: 2 business days
departments.tips: Unlike most D-clearances, a GE office clearance for GESM guarantees a seat — it cannot be issued for already-closed sections. MDA and INDS follow the same GE office routing. Check dornsife.usc.edu/ge/registration/ for the current semester's specific instructions and dates.

departments.dept_name: Materials Science (Viterbi — Mork Family Department — MASC)
departments.priority_note: Declared MFD (Mork Family Department) students receive D-clearance during mandatory advising. Non-MFD students submit via myViterbi and are lower priority. Pay attention to departmental announcements indicating when non-major requests open.
departments.clearance_required_for: MASC courses with a 'D' suffix on the section number. Courses with 'R' are open enrollment.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Process depends on your major: (1) Declared MFD/MASC students: D-clearance is issued during mandatory advising — no separate request needed. (2) Non-MFD students: submit via the myViterbi D-Clearance Request Manager at myviterbi.usc.edu. Contact mfdinfo@usc.edu for questions.
departments.contact_office: USC Viterbi — Mork Family Department of Chemical Engineering and Materials Science
departments.typical_turnaround: 2–3 business days after the non-major window opens
departments.tips: MASC is administered by the same Mork Family Department as CHEE — the same mandatory advising and myViterbi process applies. Check myViterbi departmental announcements for when non-major requests are eligible each semester.

departments.priority_note: Home department students get priority. Non-ENE students can request via myViterbi but are lower priority. Pay attention to departmental announcements on myViterbi indicating when non-major requests open.
departments.clearance_required_for: ENE courses with a 'D' suffix on the section number. Courses with 'R' are open enrollment.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Submit a request through the myViterbi D-Clearance Request Manager at myviterbi.usc.edu. ENE is listed among the Viterbi departments (alongside BME, CE, CSCI, EE, ISE, MFD) that require D-clearance requests via myViterbi. For directed research (ENE 590), use the Directed Research link in myViterbi.
departments.typical_turnaround: 2–3 business days; up to 8–10 business days during peak periods
departments.tips: ENE is confirmed as a myViterbi department. Always check the 'D' vs 'R' section suffix first. Do not contact instructors for D-clearance — all requests go through myViterbi.

departments.priority_note: No explicit priority tiers — home department students and pre-engineering students generally get priority. Non-Viterbi students should contact viterbi.studentservices@usc.edu.
departments.clearance_required_for: ENGR courses with a 'D' suffix on the section number. Confirmed for ENGR 100 and ENGR 400; always check the current Schedule of Classes note for any ENGR section.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Submit a request through the myViterbi D-Clearance Request Manager at myviterbi.usc.edu. For pre-engineering and pre-CS students, your home department advisor will provide a Microsoft Form or myViterbi instructions. For questions, contact viterbi.studentservices@usc.edu.
departments.typical_turnaround: 2–3 business days; up to 8–10 business days during peak periods
departments.tips: For internship-credit courses (ENGR 395), the process goes through Viterbi Career Connections and may take 8–10 business days during peak times. Always verify the specific ENGR section's note in Schedule of Classes since D-clearance requirements vary by course number.

departments.dept_name: Health Promotion and Disease Prevention Studies (Keck — HP, Global Health)
departments.priority_note: Declared HP/Global Health majors get priority. HP 290/490 directed research requires both advisor and faculty approval before D-clearance is issued.
departments.clearance_required_for: HP courses with a 'D' suffix on the section number. HP 290 and HP 490 (directed research) always require separate advisor + faculty approval.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Contact the Health Promotion and Disease Prevention Studies program office at bhealthy@usc.edu or call (213) 740-1060. For HP 290 and HP 490 directed research: obtain advisor and faculty approval first, then email the approval to your student-services advisor who will issue D-clearance.
departments.contact_office: USC Keck — Department of Population and Public Health Sciences
departments.typical_turnaround: Not specified; allow at least 2–3 business days
departments.tips: For directed research courses, start the advisor and faculty approval process well before registration opens — the clearance cannot be issued until both approvals are received. Always check the current Schedule of Classes note for the HP section for any term-specific contact.

departments.dept_name: Biokinesiology and Physical Therapy (USC Chan — BKPH, BKN, PT)
departments.priority_note: Most BKN and PT courses are graduate-level with major restrictions. Undergraduate access is very limited. Contact the department directly to confirm eligibility.
departments.clearance_required_for: BKN/BKPH/PT courses with a 'D' suffix on the section number. Most courses in these prefixes carry graduate or major restrictions.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Contact the Division of Biokinesiology and Physical Therapy at bknpt@usc.edu or call (323) 442-2900. There is no dedicated public undergraduate D-clearance process page — always check the current Schedule of Classes note for the specific section.
departments.contact_office: USC Chan Division of Biokinesiology and Physical Therapy — CHP 155
departments.typical_turnaround: Not specified; allow at least 2–3 business days
departments.tips: No dedicated undergraduate D-clearance process page exists — always check the Schedule of Classes note for the term-specific contact. Most BKN/PT courses are graduate; if you are an undergraduate requesting a BKN/PT course, confirm eligibility with the department before submitting any request.

departments.dept_name: Occupational Science and Occupational Therapy (USC Chan — OT, OCTH)
departments.priority_note: No explicit priority tiers — any student can contact the department. The Occupational Science minor is open to all undergraduates. The specific staff contact for D-clearance changes each term.
departments.clearance_required_for: OT courses with a 'D' suffix on the section number. Always check the Schedule of Classes note for the current term's specific contact.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Check the Schedule of Classes note for the specific OT section — the D-clearance contact changes each term. The Occupational Science minor director is Ashley Uyeshiro Simon (uyeshiro@usc.edu). For general department questions, contact otdept@usc.edu or call (323) 442-2850. D-clearance staff are located in CHP 133.
departments.contact_office: USC Chan Division of Occupational Science and Occupational Therapy — CHP 133
departments.typical_turnaround: Not specified; allow at least 2–3 business days
departments.tips: The D-clearance contact for OT courses changes every term — do not rely on a contact from a previous semester. Always look up the current term's Schedule of Classes note at classes.usc.edu before emailing anyone.

departments.priority_note: Pre-Engineering and Pre-CS students are lower priority than declared majors for all Viterbi D-clearance courses. For CSCI courses, Pre-E/Pre-CS requests are not processed until April 20 — after declared CSCI and BUAI students. For all other Viterbi departments, home department students are prioritized first.
departments.clearance_required_for: Any Viterbi course with a 'D' suffix on the section number in Schedule of Classes and WebReg.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Process depends on the course department: (1) CSCI courses: your home department advisor will provide a Microsoft Form starting March 16th each spring registration cycle. Do NOT submit via myViterbi — Pre-E/Pre-CS submissions there will be deleted. Submissions are not processed until April 20. For Microsoft Form questions, email csdept@usc.edu. (2) All other Viterbi departments (EE, AME, CEE, ISE, CHEE, MASC, ENE, ENGR, BME, ASTE): submit via the myViterbi D-Clearance Request Manager at myviterbi.usc.edu. Select the department offering the course. Do not contact course instructors for D-clearance. (3) For any questions about which process to use or if your home department has not provided a form: contact Viterbi Student Services at viterbi.studentservices@usc.edu.
departments.typical_turnaround: CSCI courses: not processed until ~April 20. All other Viterbi departments: 2–5 business days after submission, up to 8–10 during peak periods.
departments.tips: The D-clearance process differs by course department — CSCI uses a Microsoft Form, everything else uses myViterbi. Using the wrong system will result in your request being deleted. Pre-Engineering and Pre-CS students are processed after declared majors, so submit as early as the window allows and have backup courses in mind.

departments.priority_note: Varies by department — check the Dornsife hub for your specific course.
departments.clearance_required_for: Varies by department. Check the 'D' suffix on the 5-digit section number in Schedule of Classes to confirm if a course requires D-clearance.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Dornsife manages D-clearance through a central hub organized by academic cluster. Visit dornsife.usc.edu/dash/d-clearance-info/ and find your department under its cluster (Humanities, Social Sciences, Life Sciences, or Physical Sciences & Mathematics). Each department lists its own process and contact. Note: GESM, FESM, MDA, and INDS prefixes are managed by the GE office — visit dornsife.usc.edu/ge/registration/ instead. CORE prefix thematic option (TO) courses: email thematicoption@dornsife.usc.edu.
departments.contact_email: thematicoption@dornsife.usc.edu (CORE/TO courses); see hub for all others
departments.contact_office: USC Dornsife Academic Service Hubs — find your department at dornsife.usc.edu/dash/d-clearance-info/
departments.typical_turnaround: Varies by department
departments.tips: Meet with your undergraduate advisor before requesting D-clearance to confirm the course fits your academic plan. Find your advising team on your AdviseUSC account.

departments.priority_note: Restricted to enrolled IYA students. Non-IYA enrollment is extremely rare and case-by-case.
departments.clearance_required_for: All IYA courses. The academy admits a small cohort (~30 undergraduates/year) and courses are primarily restricted to enrolled IYA students.
departments.how_to_get_clearance: Contact the IYA program office directly at iovine-young@usc.edu. Explain your interest and how the course fits your academic goals. There is no formal public D-clearance process for non-IYA undergraduates — enrollment is rare and case-by-case.
departments.typical_turnaround: Not formally defined; contact office directly
departments.tips: Non-IYA enrollment is extremely limited. A compelling interdisciplinary project rationale or a direct connection to an IYA faculty member improves your chances. Generic requests are unlikely to succeed.
